reviews.content: I am a first time mother and want a natural childbirth. I got this book after looking at many natural childbirth literature lists and this seemed to be on every list I found. I am estatic that I got this book and highly recommend it to any first time mother and every woman who is pregnant no matter how many times. The birth stories were inspiring and compelling. It has brought me to a realization that our womanly bodies are capable of doing this feat of child labor without interventions. It has made me less fearful of child labor without pain meds and has made me stronger at my convictions of not wanting interventions (unless emergent) or medications. Please read for any woman who is pregnant or is thinking of becoming pregnant. It is a very easy read as well, I read it in two days!!!!

reviews.content: For ANYONE who will at some time in their life experience pregnancy, labor and birth, whether actively or as a supporter. The first half of the book shares beautiful, personal stories of labor and birth, which have taken place under the care of Ina May or one of her fellow Farm-midwives. As the author, Ina May also adds her reasonings of why certain situations occurred and how she safely helped the mothers through them. The second half reveals facts and statistics of the many procedures that often accompany labor and birth from BOTH the medical AND the midwifery world of labor and birth in America compared with other developed countries. It is a warm, loving, nurturing book that supports and informs readers of the natural process of labor and birth that a woman's and a baby's body endures, without too many big or science-based words. It shines light onto the myths about how long a woman takes to labor, how long into a pregnancy one can be before inducing, how UNNECESSARY the majority of cesarian sections are in our country, and much much more!!! It is FASCINATING, APPALLING (when you read of the unnecessary statistics-that leave moms in MORE and LONGER-lasting pain than the actual birth would have-that occur in hospitals), UPLIFTING, BEAUTIFUL, PROFOUND and AMAZING. I say it is FEARLESS because prior to reading this book, I was always afraid of the pain that was associated with giving birth. When I finished it, I was SO EMPOWERED I could have given birth that minute:) This book opened my eyes to a WHOLE NEW WORLD of childbirth that works WONDERFULLY WELL when it is approached with the utmost love, compassion, naturalness and awareness, to ensure the safety or both mother and child. It INSTILLS POWER into the mother that she is capable of having a pleasurable birthing experience, one that is potentially pain-free! It is a MUST-READ for anyone that is open and willing to accept the most AMAZING process of our existence:) I say this because I do know one person who I've bought this for and she wasn't too psyched on the idea... but she is also afraid of giving birth and wasn't open enough to let go of her fear, which the book explains is unnecessary, and to surrender to the PERFECT PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESS that she will endure! Everyone else I've bought this book for, they have LOVED it, and felt empowered as well, and recommend it to their friends, as well! I hope you enjoy it as much as I did...

reviews.content:
The birth stories in the beginning are warm and empowering however all take place on the farm there are no positive stories from elsewhere. The author then dives into the negatives of obstetrics versus the positives off midwifery. . . in my case there are no midwives around and it made me feel almost like a prisoner of my options. She then delves into birth how you can do it which i found absolutely worth the read! Then however,she falls back into discussing midwifery. . telling us about past midwives an their experiences. . i felt compelled to skip pages. I did not for fear of overlooking something useful and was dissappointed. The final chapters talk about our faulty obstetrics again and how we should strive to improve.
Overall this book had 30% information i wanted 30% babble about multiple midwiferies and their statics 30% absolutely horrifing information about obstetrical intervention and why to not go to them 10% amazingly personal stories of strength and how to have faith in your own body
